title: One calm context tray
mechanism: For a busy caregiver, constraint-first disclosure reserves one glass navigation tray for date, routine scope and Details. MainPageHeader removes separate switches into this tray; section headers mirror its summary and task rows use a Details button.
visible: Title, selected period, scope label, completion and essential deadline.
disclosed: Tray expands existing period navigator, accumulated switch, duration breakdown and diagnostic; list and section options retain named routes; task panel contains all metadata editors. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px buttons, semantic expansion, restored focus; keyboard access and opaque glass fallback.
benefit: A single stable place carries supporting information.
risk: Combining scope and date could imply they share state.
verification: Check independent scope/date callbacks, duration, menus, completion and 320/375px.

title: Exception gutter
mechanism: A caregiver's adversarial hierarchy treats hidden overdue context as a failure. Keep a narrow textual exception gutter for out-of-period dates, accumulated origin and urgent expiry; normal metadata moves into task Details. Headers show selected period and plain summaries; section options remain visible.
visible: Titles, completion, selected period and explicit exceptional context.
disclosed: Details reveal duration, frequency, price, links and time-of-day; header summaries open existing diagnostics and scope controls. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px named buttons and focus rings; exception text is never color-only.
benefit: Quiet everyday rows while retaining consequential differences.
risk: Too many exceptional tasks can refill the gutter.
verification: Test overdue, historical, partial and all-done states, metadata callbacks and mobile wrapping.

title: Section action shelf
mechanism: The household organizer inverts toolbar clutter: place section actions in a disclosed shelf directly below the section title rather than competing beside its count. Header retains global navigation and list options; tasks retain completion plus a named metadata opener.
visible: Section title, total count, collapse button and Actions trigger; task title and meaningful date.
disclosed: Shelf contains existing section menu route, include-frequency control, duration breakdown and start callback; global options and task metadata remain available. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px shelf controls; expansion order follows document order; no hover dependency.
benefit: Scope of every action becomes spatially explicit.
risk: Open shelves can make long lists taller.
verification: Check sibling actions never affect another section, drag behavior, accumulated scope and keyboard collapse.

title: Inherited context line
mechanism: For shared-house context-first constraints, print selected period and included frequencies once above each contiguous section block. Task rows display only metadata that differs from that line. Page header provides source context; section headers show inheritance exceptions and a context button.
visible: Period line, scope phrase, counts, task completion and differing deadlines.
disclosed: Context button exposes period navigation, include controls and duration; task Details always expose complete original metadata; Options retain all menus. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px named context buttons; task accessible descriptions include inherited context.
benefit: Removes repeated information while making the source legible.
risk: Inherited context could be mistaken for a task's own setting.
verification: Verify differing frequencies, historical dates, same-period tasks, metadata editors and narrow wrapping.

title: Two separate disclosures
mechanism: The organizer's adversarial disclosure separates information from commands: every page, section and task has a Details route and an Options route, eliminating ambiguity over whether summaries change state. Keep completion outside both.
visible: Titles, selected period, count, completion, Details and Options.
disclosed: Details show full duration, accumulated breakdown and all metadata editors; Options retain existing list/section/task command menus and scope toggles with current state. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: Each route is 44px, visibly labeled, keyboard operable and focus-restoring.
benefit: Users can inspect shared work without accidentally invoking commands.
risk: Two routes may still occupy considerable width.
verification: Test no metadata opener completes a task, every original command remains reachable and 320px layout stacks.

title: Household ledger
mechanism: A first-principles household view uses an aligned ledger: page header is a caption, section headers are ledger dividers, task rows share a title column and one quiet context column. At mobile width the context column becomes a disclosed line.
visible: Caption with period, section count, completion and a concise deadline or context value.
disclosed: A Context button expands complete metadata; summary footer opens duration and routine diagnostics; named menus preserve all commands and scope settings. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px controls, semantic lists, tabular counters and readable opaque rows.
benefit: Shared alignment replaces many independent badge shapes.
risk: Fixed columns can squeeze long household titles.
verification: Verify long titles, nested rows, price/duration totals, historical reference dates and desktop/mobile conversion.

title: Start scope gate
mechanism: For constrained work time, one glass Start button opens a compact scope gate showing existing duration and included routines before calling the unchanged sequence callback. Headers stop duplicating duration beside unrelated controls; section Start uses the same scoped gate; task completion stays immediate.
visible: Title, selected date, current scope and Start; task title, completion and deadline.
disclosed: Gate contains duration breakdown, accumulated toggle and Start confirmation; Options and task Details retain remaining editors and commands. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px gate actions, dialog focus trap and restored trigger; reduced-motion opening.
benefit: Work effort becomes visible exactly before starting.
risk: Adds one step to sequence launch.
verification: Verify Start uses current scope, disabling rules, estimates, all menus and task completion.

title: Time accounting sentence
mechanism: The worker's adversarial context design replaces compact unexplained numbers with one sentence: estimated active time plus parallel time, explicitly tied to the selected period and scope. Sections repeat only their own sentence; tasks show time through a sentence opener.
visible: Title, chosen period, scope and 'Estimated 35 min' summary; task completion and deadlines.
disclosed: Summary opens existing DurationInfoCard with own/subtask and accumulated splits; Details retain price, schedule, links; Options retain commands. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px summary buttons, descriptive names, tabular figures and wrapping text.
benefit: Prevents parallel or historical work from looking like current active time.
risk: Long explanatory sentences can consume height.
verification: Verify active/parallel distinction, completed totals, inherited duration, historical dates and 320px.

title: Read and plan tabs
mechanism: First-principles disclosure for constrained workers divides supporting header content into two labeled tabs: Tasks is default; Plan shows scope, duration, selected-period navigation and diagnostics. Section Plan disclosures sit inline; task Details remain local.
visible: Tasks tab shows title, selected period, scope summary, completion and deadline.
disclosed: Plan exposes existing inclusion switch and breakdowns; global Options remains visible; task Details exposes every metadata editor and link. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px tabs with keyboard semantics, visible selected state and no loss of task focus.
benefit: Task reading and planning each receive a coherent surface.
risk: Tab changes could obscure the active planning scope.
verification: Check shared scope state across tabs, all callbacks, date persistence and small-screen fit.

title: Steady metadata rail
mechanism: A worker inverts badge movement by reserving one fixed metadata rail under each task title. It contains a single context summary button rather than variable chips; expanding it inserts details below. Headers use the same fixed summary rail; sections preserve collapse and Options.
visible: Task title, completion, chosen-period header and one wrapping summary.
disclosed: Rail opens all metadata with direct duration/price/date/frequency editing and time-of-day cycling; section/page rails expose breakdowns and scope controls. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px rail opener, bounded transitions, no animation under reduced motion.
benefit: Stable control positions support fast scanning as data changes.
risk: Reserved rail space can waste room on sparse tasks.
verification: Verify empty metadata, changing completion/counts, subtask totals, menus and virtualized row sizing.

title: Completion lane
mechanism: The weekly cleaner's adversarial action design gives completion a dedicated leading lane, with all inspection controls trailing. Header and section Start remain labeled; duration and accumulated details enter a separate inspection drawer.
visible: Leading completion targets, titles, selected week, included-scope phrase and Start.
disclosed: Trailing Details opens task metadata; Inspection opens existing duration diagnostics and inclusion controls; Options exposes unchanged menus. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px nonoverlapping lanes, descriptive completion names and keyboard order.
benefit: Reduces accidental editing while marking many household tasks complete.
risk: Trailing controls may be distant on wide screens.
verification: Test partial repetitions, blocked tasks, accidental propagation, scope toggles and narrow lanes.

title: Week notebook
mechanism: A first-principles cleaner context view uses a notebook composition: a dated heading, plain section headings, ruled task rows and small prose annotations. Replace badges with text; keep a clearly marked Details link-sized button for each row.
visible: Selected week heading, routine-scope phrase, section counts, task titles and exceptional due dates.
disclosed: Header annotation opens navigator and diagnostics; section annotation opens duration and scope; task Details holds full metadata and editors; menus stay named. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px controls despite small text; headings and list semantics; monochrome contrast.
benefit: One editorial rhythm makes cleaning work feel ordered.
risk: Plain text affordances may look noninteractive.
verification: Verify focus/pressed styling, duration data, all menus, 320px text fit and completion.

title: Unfolded cleaning checklist
mechanism: The cleaner inverts disclosure by initially showing only section titles with meaningful counts; opening a section reveals tasks plus one shared context footer. Existing section collapse state drives this, avoiding new completion logic.
visible: Page title, selected period, scope, section headings/counts and disclosure controls.
disclosed: Expanded section footer exposes duration, inclusion and Options; task Details exposes frequency, date, price, time-of-day and links. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px collapse controls, aria-expanded, focus stays on heading and reduced-motion expansion.
benefit: Long routine lists begin as an understandable map.
risk: Collapsed tasks require an extra step to complete.
verification: Verify category collapse contracts, nested sections, include mode, historical dates and menu access.

title: One material per hierarchy
mechanism: A cleaner's constrained hierarchy uses glass only for the page navigation band, matte section backgrounds and unboxed task rows. Count, scope and duration become plain text links; only expanded details acquire an elevated panel.
visible: Navigation, selected period, titles, counts and completion; small scope summary.
disclosed: 44px Details routes reveal all metadata and original editors; existing duration cards, diagnostics, include switches and menus stay reachable. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: Contrast fallback, visible focus, no nested blur and scoped reduced-motion transitions.
benefit: Material distinguishes navigation from work without adding controls.
risk: Flat sections might lose grouping on busy backgrounds.
verification: Verify light/dark contrast, counts, menu layering, accumulated scope and 320/375px.

title: Maintenance action itinerary
mechanism: A maintenance planner's first-principles action view makes existing Start sequence the anchor of a section itinerary. Header shows selected month; sections show ordered tasks and a final Start/Details footer; task completion remains individually available.
visible: Month, scope, section title/count, task titles and completion.
disclosed: Itinerary footer opens estimates, accumulated breakdown and Start; Options preserves management; task Details preserves every metadata action. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px controls, list order remains unchanged, semantic footer and restored focus.
benefit: Planning and execution connect to the exact section.
risk: Footers below long sections can be missed.
verification: Verify global and section Start scope, duration, ordering, keyboard routes and narrow overflow.

title: Period provenance captions
mechanism: The planner inverts context redundancy by giving each section a provenance caption: selected month plus included shorter frequencies. Tasks omit repeated frequency badges only when matching; differing frequency remains written out.
visible: Header period, section provenance, counts, task completion and mismatching dates/frequency.
disclosed: Provenance button opens navigator, scope settings and diagnostic; task Details exposes full metadata including hidden matches; Options remains available. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px caption target, full accessible context and text-based distinctions.
benefit: Shows where accumulated maintenance work comes from.
risk: Repeated provenance captions can be lengthy.
verification: Verify own/accumulated totals, mixed-frequency sections, custom cycles, reference dates and mobile wrapping.

title: Maintenance inspector dock
mechanism: Constraint-first disclosure uses one inspector dock attached below the page header on desktop and a sheet on mobile. Page, section and task Details select the inspector's subject without duplicating panels; completion stays on rows.
visible: Titles, selected period, scope, counts and labeled Details triggers.
disclosed: Inspector shows existing duration/diagnostic views or complete task metadata, with focused editors; Options keeps all original commands and inclusion controls. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px triggers, subject heading announced, focus restoration and no hidden tab stops.
benefit: One support surface keeps a large maintenance list quiet.
risk: Subject switches could cause edits to the wrong item.
verification: Verify subject IDs, callback targets, focus, historical period and sheet fit at 320px.

title: Persistent scope watermark
mechanism: The planner's adversarial hierarchy treats mistaken accumulated scope as the main hazard. A restrained textual scope watermark sits underneath the page title and every section whose scope differs; other metadata stays quiet.
visible: Selected month, explicit own/combined scope text, titles and completion.
disclosed: Watermark opens scope toggle with current state plus duration and diagnostic; task Details opens original metadata; list/section Options remains visible. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px watermark button, text rather than color signal, semantic state and keyboard access.
benefit: Scope survives even when supporting controls are disclosed.
risk: Too many differing scopes can repeat context.
verification: Verify section/global independence, own-done/accumulated-pending state, menus, dates and small widths.

title: Shopping receipt footer
mechanism: The budget planner inverts action placement using a receipt footer: page and section costs live below their scoped content rather than beside titles; task row preserves completion and a compact price-edit button where meaningful.
visible: Titles, completion, pending price, selected-period context where applicable and footer trigger.
disclosed: Receipt expands pending/paid/original totals and quantity/subtask splits; Details retains other metadata; Options retains management and accumulated controls for routine contexts. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px price/footer controls, tabular numerals and semantic cost descriptions.
benefit: Purchasing actions and subtotals align with their scope.
risk: Users may overlook a footer below a long list.
verification: Verify shopping duration suppression, quantity multiplication, paid totals, task editors and mobile layout.

title: Dual context receipt
mechanism: A constrained budget context design shows two plain receipt lines: current cost state and temporal/routine scope. Header carries total; sections carry subtotal; tasks keep one price summary and completion, with glass reserved for navigation.
visible: Pending euros, selected period/scope, titles and completion.
disclosed: Receipt line opens pending/paid split and existing duration where applicable; Details retains full task data and edit callbacks; Options retains every command. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px summary buttons, readable matte text and no color-only cost status.
benefit: Separates money from time without a field of badges.
risk: Dual summaries still add height in nonshopping views.
verification: Verify price/subtask calculations, nonshopping duration, include modes, historical period and 320px.

title: Explicit field chooser
mechanism: The budget planner's adversarial disclosure forbids ambiguous whole-row editing. Each task has a named 'Edit details' button opening a field chooser; page and section Summary buttons similarly choose Cost, Time or Routine before existing panels.
visible: Title, completion, cost or deadline summary and named edit opener.
disclosed: Chooser routes directly to original duration/price/date/frequency editors, time-of-day toggle and links; header options preserve management and inclusion. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px chooser rows, dialog naming, Escape and focus return.
benefit: Hidden metadata still has a predictable editing route.
risk: A chooser can add a step to simple edits.
verification: Test all field routes, quantity, subtasks, inclusion, diagnostics and task completion without propagation.

title: Value-first typographic rows
mechanism: A first-principles budget hierarchy makes each monetary total a quiet aligned numeral, removing individual badge containers. Page total is largest; section subtotal medium; task amount smallest. Temporal/routine context remains plain captions.
visible: Titles, aligned cost numbers, completion, selected period and scope caption.
disclosed: Numeric buttons open complete cost splits; Details retains all task metadata; summary opens time/routine panels; Options keeps commands and inclusion controls. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px numeric hit areas, tabular digits, labels and visible focus.
benefit: Clear relative scale communicates scope without decorative chips.
risk: Strong cost hierarchy can dominate nonshopping tasks.
verification: Verify conditional shopping context, paid amounts, duration preservation, long titles and narrow stacking.

title: Section breadcrumb actions
mechanism: For deeply nested sections, constrained action hierarchy places current section path in a compact breadcrumb action strip. Page retains global Options; each section has one Actions button whose panel starts with its full path; task completion stays local.
visible: Page period/scope, section name/count, breadcrumb context and completion.
disclosed: Actions panel preserves section menu, inclusion, duration and start; task Details includes parent path plus complete original metadata. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px breadcrumb/action targets, wrapping paths and semantic navigation only where supported.
benefit: Prevents acting on the wrong nested section.
risk: Breadcrumb paths can occupy several lines.
verification: Verify deeply nested scope IDs, drag/nesting, callback target, historical dates and 320px overflow.

title: Depth-independent context rows
mechanism: An adversarial nested context design stops indentation from consuming metadata width. Section titles retain a small depth cue, while period and scope appear in a full-width context row below; tasks likewise place Details outside indentation.
visible: Section hierarchy cue, full-width context text, counts, titles and completion.
disclosed: Context row exposes period, duration and inclusion; Options opens existing section menu; task Details retains every editor and navigation link. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px independent targets; heading order and full path accessible name.
benefit: Metadata remains readable even at deep nesting.
risk: Reduced indentation can weaken parent-child recognition.
verification: Verify five-level nesting, screen-reader path, drag affordances, mixed periods and mobile widths.

title: Outline with inline inspector
mechanism: First-principles nested disclosure uses an outline: sections collapse normally, and a section Details control inserts one inline inspector before its tasks. Tasks each disclose their own metadata without creating cards within cards.
visible: Outline headings/counts, selected period/scope, completion and Details.
disclosed: Inline inspector includes estimates, accumulated control and section Options; task details contains all original metadata actions; global menu remains visible. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px controls, aria-controls, unboxed separators and reduced-motion resizing.
benefit: Supporting information stays beside the correct hierarchy node.
risk: Many open inspectors could become visually dense.
verification: Verify collapse/disclosure independence, virtualized sizes, all actions, referenceDate and 320px.

title: Ancestor summary transfer
mechanism: A nested user inverts repeated hierarchy summaries by placing aggregate duration/count in the highest expanded ancestor and showing descendant summaries only through Details. Each descendant retains its own name, scope exception and Options route; task metadata is likewise disclosed.
visible: Ancestor totals, descendant titles, scope differences, selected date and completion.
disclosed: Details returns every descendant estimate and breakdown, inclusion control and metadata editor; Options preserves existing commands. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px named targets; accessible descriptions state aggregate scope; no altered calculations.
benefit: Removes repeated totals while preserving ownership cues.
risk: Aggregate totals may be misread as own-section totals.
verification: Verify no double counting changes, parent/child labels, collapse transitions, duration and mobile menus.

title: Return-to-work checkpoint
mechanism: An adversarial action view for missed periods places a compact checkpoint before Start: selected historical/current period and own-versus-accumulated scope remain explicit. Sections have scoped checkpoints; tasks retain immediate completion and visible period exceptions.
visible: Checkpoint, title, counts, scope and task completion.
disclosed: Checkpoint opens existing navigator, diagnostics, accumulated setting and estimates; Start calls original callback; Details and Options preserve all remaining actions. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px controls, explicit date labels, focus management and unchanged completion semantics.
benefit: Returning users can understand what they are about to act on.
risk: Extra checkpoint may feel repetitive across sections.
verification: Verify missed periods, partial targets, selected dates, scope callback independence and 320px.

title: Origin ledger
mechanism: First-principles return context uses a plain origin ledger under the header: own routines and included shorter frequencies as named rows with counts. Sections show one source summary; task metadata becomes a Details disclosure.
visible: Selected period, ledger summary, titles, completion and exceptional due dates.
disclosed: Ledger expansion shows original routine breakdown, duration and diagnostic; section Details exposes inclusion; task Details retains all editors; Options preserves menus. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px ledger opener, text labels, semantic table/list and tabular counts.
benefit: Accumulated work stops looking like unexplained arithmetic.
risk: Source rows could be mistaken for overdue backlog.
verification: Verify labels match actual frequency accumulation, historical referenceDate, all-done states and widths.

title: Context before options
mechanism: The returning user inverts menu-first disclosure: a Context button opens a read-only summary first, with separate named links to Change period, Included routines, Estimates and Options. Sections and tasks use the same structure with their actual available fields.
visible: Title, selected period, scope summary, completion and Context.
disclosed: Summary provides full data and routes to unchanged navigator, toggles, menus and focused task editors; no summary click directly mutates. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px links, accessible dialog heading and reliable focus return.
benefit: Inspection is safe while remembering the app after absence.
risk: Extra routing increases taps to management commands.
verification: Verify every preserved command route, changing context freshness, historical dates and mobile sheet.

title: Current-context ribbon
mechanism: Constraint-first hierarchy gives the selected period and routine scope one narrow glass ribbon below navigation, while all task and section data stays matte. Ribbon persists during scrolling; section scope deviations remain inline textual exceptions.
visible: Persistent period/scope ribbon, titles, counts, completion and deviations.
disclosed: Ribbon opens navigator, inclusion and diagnostic; section Details opens duration and local scope; task Details exposes full metadata; Options retains commands. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px ribbon controls, contrast fallback, reduced motion and focus rings.
benefit: Temporal context remains present without repeating large header blocks.
risk: Persistent ribbon reduces available mobile height.
verification: Verify sticky overlaps, historical context, local/global scope, completion, all menus and 320px.

title: Historical action caption
mechanism: For history review, first-principles action hierarchy places the selected historical period immediately above completion and restoration controls as a caption. Page and section action labels include their actual scope; supporting totals move behind Details.
visible: Historical date caption, task titles, completion/restoration and scope text.
disclosed: Details reveals duration, price, routine diagnostics and all metadata editors; Options preserves commands, accumulated settings and existing exports where present. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px actions, explicit accessible dates, visible focus and unchanged callbacks.
benefit: Actions stay understandable during review of past work.
risk: Repeated date captions may feel heavy.
verification: Verify historical referenceDate propagation, completed restoration, scope toggles, exports and narrow rows.

title: History margin notes
mechanism: The historical reviewer inverts current-date assumptions through margin notes: header gives selected period, section captions give period-specific status, and task notes expose differing due dates. All decorative capsules become plain text; complete metadata is disclosed.
visible: Selected period, section context status, differing due dates, titles and completion.
disclosed: Context-note buttons open navigator/diagnostic and duration; task Details retains every editor and link; named Options retains management and inclusion. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px note hit areas, noncolor date cues, wrapping text and restored focus.
benefit: Period-specific explanations remain visible during historical scanning.
risk: Margin layout may require stacking at small widths.
verification: Verify rollover labels use referenceDate, past mixed frequencies, all-done/partial states and 320/375px.

title: Historical evidence sheet
mechanism: Constraint-first historical disclosure uses one Evidence sheet with tabs for Period, Routine and Estimates, opened from header/section Details. Task Details opens full original metadata with the same selected-period caption. Navigation alone receives glass.
visible: Historical period caption, scope, titles, counts, completion and Details.
disclosed: Sheet retains navigator, diagnostic, accumulated controls and duration splits; Options preserves commands; task editors and links keep original callbacks. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
access: 44px tab/buttons, semantic tabs, focus trap/return, opaque fallback and reduced motion.
benefit: Several historical signals become one inspectable supporting surface.
risk: Tabs can hide cross-category relationships.
verification: Verify period persists across tabs, own/accumulated totals, focused editors, completion and mobile fit.
